Apply stage 3 (QC + calibration) across the casts under root.

Reads each cast’s stage-2 file, applies stage3(), and writes a new stage3/<stem>_stage3.nc — never in place. Reads are strict: a cast with no stage-2 file is skipped with a warning (its soak/deck flags were never applied, so QC’ing it would manufacture a product whose filename lies). Called by ctdcast.processors.process() with stage=3.

Parameters:

  • root – The CTD stage root (ctd_root). Stage files live under root/stage2/ … root/stage3/.

  • force – Rewrite the stage-3 file even when it already exists. Without force, a cast whose stage3/<stem>_stage3.nc exists is skipped.

  • dry_run – Print what would be processed without writing any output.

  • cast_tags – If given, process only casts selected by these zero-padded tags (e.g. {"042"}), matched on the parsed cast identity.

  • cruise_info – The config cruise_info: block. When it declares data_mode: D, each stage-3 file is stamped data_mode = "D"; if no calibration was actually applied the delayed-mode claim is unsupported, so the cast is named in a warning and the gap recorded in history.

  • **kw – Passed to stage3() (e.g. cruise_cfg).

Returns:

Number of stage-3 files written (0 for dry_run).

Return type:

int

Raises:

FileNotFoundError – If root does not exist or is not a directory.

ctdcast.processors.stage3.stage3(ds: Dataset, cruise_cfg: dict | None = None, *, cast_number: int | None = None, cast_label: str = '?', context: StepContext | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Apply the configured processing steps, derived variables and QC to a per-cast Dataset.

Applies, in order:

  1. The per-sensor conductivity slope and offset (data_processing.slope_offset), as Sea-Bird applies them when it converts the raw counts.

  2. data_processing.steps, in the order listed: wildedit and loopedit (ctdcast.processors.editing), filter and window_filter (ctdcast.processors.filtering), alignctd and celltm (ctdcast.processors.corrections.apply_corrections()), from ctdcast.processors.steps.STEPS. A step ctdcast does not apply yet is skipped (run refuses it unless data_processing.allow_unapplied), with a warning and a history note. The order they ran in is written to the data_processing_steps attribute.

  3. Re-derives practical salinity whenever a step changed conductivity, temperature or pressure.

  4. Derives ctd_oxygen from the SBE 43 voltage on a cast that carries oxygen_raw_<N> and no converted oxygen (ctdcast.processors.corrections.derive_oxygen()), with the window in data_processing.oxygen.

  5. Two-tier gross-range QC and the QARTOD spike test, on the corrected values, using the package defaults merged with qc.gross_range / qc.spike.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Per-cast Dataset (dim=time), already through stage1 and stage2.

  • cruise_cfg (dict or None) – The settings from ctdcast.config.layout.processing_view(): data_processing and qc are read here.

  • cast_number (int or None) – The cast’s number, for per-cast-range values.

  • cast_label (str) – How the cast is named in warnings (e.g. "011").

  • context (StepContext, optional) – Filled in as the steps run (Wild Edit’s marks, Loop Edit’s scans), for the products made from this cast in the same run.

Returns:

New Dataset; input is not mutated. Values read from a file (stored float32) are computed on in float64.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Stage QC — two-tier gross-range and spike flagging.

Each test has a suspect tier (QARTOD flag 3) and a fail tier (flag 4); the wider fail bound wins, and a more-severe flag is never downgraded (worst-flag-wins). Non-finite samples are marked missing (flag 9), not pass. The thresholds applied are recorded as attributes on each {var}_qc companion so the treatment reconstructs from the file alone. Operates on per-cast Datasets (dim=time); call after apply_stage2 so the soak/deck flags are already present.

Note: config overrides are trusted, not validated — a suspect range set wider than its fail range is accepted as given (ioos_qc would reject it).

Two-tier gross-range QC: flag 3 outside suspect bounds, flag 4 outside fail.

Creates {var}_qc companions (int8, 1=pass) as needed, sets suspect (3) then fail (4) so the wider fail bound wins, and records the applied bounds (qc_gross_range_{suspect,fail}_{min,max}) on each companion so the report reads them back. A more-severe flag is never downgraded.

Parameters:

  • ds – Per-cast Dataset (dim=time); input is not mutated.

  • thresholds – Config overrides with suspect and/or fail sub-dicts of {var: (min, max)}, merged over GROSS_RANGE_SUSPECT / GROSS_RANGE_FAIL.

xr.Dataset

ctdcast.processors.qc.apply_spike_test(ds: Dataset, thresholds: dict | None = None) → Dataset[source]

Two-tier QARTOD spike test: flag 3 above the suspect threshold, flag 4 above fail.

The spike metric for an interior sample is |v[i] - (v[i-1] + v[i+1]) / 2|; endpoints are not evaluated. Records the thresholds (qc_spike_{suspect,fail}_threshold) on each {var}_qc. Fluorescence and turbidity have no spike test (natural fine-scale variability). A more-severe flag is never downgraded.

Parameters:

  • ds – Per-cast Dataset (dim=time); input is not mutated.

  • thresholds – Config overrides with suspect and/or fail sub-dicts of {var: threshold}, merged over SPIKE_SUSPECT / SPIKE_FAIL.

xr.Dataset

Return the cast’s pressure, NaN where pressure_qc is fail (4) or missing (9).

Pressure places every other value in the cast: it picks the deepest scan, the bins and the grid. A scan whose pressure failed a test (a Wild Edit mark, a gross-range fail) has no trustworthy depth, so it is left out of all three, as SBE Data Processing drops a scan Wild Edit marked. Without pressure_qc the pressure is returned as it is.

Parameters:

ds (xarray.Dataset) – A cast with pressure and, optionally, pressure_qc.

Returns:

Pressure as float, a copy.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Cruise-level profile compiler: per-cast netCDF → profiles.nc.

Reads all per-cast netCDF files in a directory, splits each into downcast and upcast halves, bins to a common 1-dbar grid, and writes a single (N_PROF × pressure) netCDF. The converters module re-exports build_profiles for backward compatibility.

ctdcast.processors.profiles.build_profiles(nc_dir: Path, profiles_path: Path, *, force: bool = False, gebco_path: Path | None = None, dbar: int = 1, cruise_info: dict | None = None, cruise_cfg: dict | None = None, refuse_catalog_less: bool = False) → bool[source]

Compile per-cast netCDF files into a single profiles.nc on a dbar-spaced grid.

Reads all *.nc files in nc_dir, splits each cast into downcast and upcast halves, bins to a common dbar-dbar pressure grid (default 1 dbar), and writes a single (N_PROF × pressure) netCDF. N_PROF is a plain integer index (0, 1, 2, …); cast identity is carried by cast_number, cast_suffix, and cast_direction variables. The bin spacing is recorded in the pressure_spacing_dbar global attribute so the gridding can be reconstructed from the output file alone.

Per-cast scalar variables added to the output:

  • max_pressure_dbar — maximum pressure recorded over the full cast.

  • gebco_depth_m — GEBCO bathymetry depth (m, positive down) at the max-pressure lat/lon position; NaN when gebco_path is None or the file is unavailable.

The altimeter channel (when present in the input files) is binned onto the 1-dbar grid as a standard 2-D variable.

Samples carrying a QARTOD fail (4) or missing (9) flag on their {var}_qc companion are NaN-masked before binning, so failed data does not enter the bin means; a suspect (3) sample is kept, as in a product’s Bin Average. Each science variable records how many finite input samples it carried (qc_input_samples) and how many were excluded (qc_excluded_samples).

Parameters:

  • nc_dir – Directory containing per-cast netCDF files.

  • profiles_path – Output path for the compiled profiles netCDF.

  • force – Overwrite an existing profiles_path.

  • gebco_path – Path to a GEBCO_2025.nc file. Used to look up water depth at each cast’s max-pressure position. Pass cfg.gebco_path when calling from report generation code. Silently omitted when None.

  • dbar – Vertical bin spacing (dbar) of the output grid. Default 1. Use 2 (or more) to average adjacent pressure levels together, reducing per-level noise when the raw scan resolution does not justify a 1-dbar grid.

  • cruise_info – The cruise_info: mapping from the cruise config. Supplies the cruise id (so the compiled file is not labelled UNK), the authored discovery fields, people, embargo, and the ship/start_date from which the EXPOCODE coordinate is derived. Coverage bounds and creation time are computed from the data, not taken from here.

  • cruise_cfg – The settings from ctdcast.config.layout.processing_view(). Used only to reconcile the preferred_pair / preferred_oxygen declaration against the per-cast sensor serials (validate_preferred()); a declared range crossing a hardware swap, or a swap segment the declaration does not cover, is warned — never an error, never a block on compiling.

  • refuse_catalog_less – Policy for a CTD cast whose per-cast file carries no SENSOR_* catalog (it predates sensor provenance). The default False is the library behaviour: warn once, name the files, and stamp the admission into the output so the gap is visible in the file itself. The pipeline driver (ctdcast process --stage profiles and ctdcast run) passes True so the compile refuses instead — at the point a product is shipped, re-running stage 1 to build the catalog is the actionable fix.

Returns:

True if profiles.nc was written; False if skipped (existed, force=False).

Return type:

bool

Raises:

ValueError – If no recognised cast files are found in nc_dir, or if refuse_catalog_less is True and any cast carries no sensor catalog.

Reconcile the preferred-sensor declaration against the per-cast sensor serials.

Runs validate_preferred() for every group and returns the collected messages — it does not emit them, so each caller chooses how (the profiles compile re-raises them as warnings; ctdcast validate collects them into its own report). Reporting at both call sites catches a bad declaration before compiling. The conditions reported: a declared range crossing a hardware-segment boundary, and a derived segment the declaration does not cover. A partial declaration is a normal mid-processing state, never an error.

list of str

Read the SENSOR_* catalog stage 1 built, from any per-cast stage file.

Stage 1 writes a dimensionless SENSOR_<TYPE>_<SERIAL> variable per physical sensor, carrying its sensor_role and sensor_channel. This module reads that catalog back — the inverse of the stage-1 builder — so every later step (the stage-3 preferred-sensor stamp, the profiles.nc compile, and ctdcast validate) shares one reader and no stage imports a later stage.

ctdcast.processors.sensor_catalog.catalog_by_cast_number(per_identity: Iterable[tuple[tuple[int, str], list[dict]]]) → tuple[dict[int, list[dict]], list[str]][source]

Collapse per-identity catalogs to one per cast number, flagging sibling mismatches.

The preferred-sensor declaration is per cast number, so a plain cast and its lettered sibling (010 / 010b) share one declaration and collapse to one entry here. When two siblings sharing a number carry different sensor serials, the per-number declaration cannot distinguish them — a warning naming both casts is returned so the operator knows the reconciliation treats them as one.

Parameters:

per_identity (iterable of ((int, str), list of dict)) – ((cast_number, cast_suffix), records) pairs — one per cast identity, records as returned by read_cast_sensor_catalog().

Returns:

tuple of (dict of {int – The catalog keyed by cast number (a later sibling overwrites an earlier one), and the sibling-mismatch warning strings (empty when no number has differing siblings).

Return type:

list of dict}, list of str)

ctdcast.processors.sensor_catalog.read_cast_sensor_catalog(ds: Dataset) → list[dict][source]

Return one record per SENSOR_* catalog entry in a per-cast dataset.

Reads the catalog stage 1 built: each dimensionless SENSOR_<TYPE>_<SERIAL> variable, taking its sensor_role and sensor_channel off the entry itself (not off the data variables). A sensor with no stored variable — pH, a transmissometer — is therefore read exactly like one that has a variable, which is what lets the compile aggregate without re-parsing the CNV header.

Parameters:

ds (xarray.Dataset) – A per-cast dataset carrying the stage-1 SENSOR_* catalog variables.

Returns:

One record per catalog entry, each with name (the catalog variable name, already resolved at stage 1), role, channel (int, or -1 if unstated) and attrs (the full entry attributes, verbatim). [] when the cast carries no catalog.

Return type:

list of dict

Stamped history notes for the processing stages.

Every stage records what it did — and the parameters it used — as a line in the CF history global attribute, so the treatment is reconstructable from the output file alone. Because each stage reads its predecessor and copies its attributes, history accumulates: stage 3 inherits the stage 1 and stage 2 lines and appends its own.

The format, from one helper so it stays consistent, is:

<timestamp> <producer> <version> <stage>: <note>

joined with newlines. ctdcast’s own stages use the defaults — an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, producer ctdcast — giving <ISO-8601 UTC> ctdcast <version> <stage>. An upstream Sea-Bird step overrides producer ("SBE Data Processing"), timestamp (the tool’s own verbatim stamp, no Z) and the stage field (the module name, e.g. celltm), so a stage-1 file’s history shows Sea-Bird’s own lines alongside ctdcast’s.

ctdcast.processors.history.PL_CONVERTED = 'Instrument data that has been converted to geophysical values'

OceanSITES reference-table-3 processing_level values, verbatim. A variable can carry several at once (converted, then calibrated, then flagged): they are joined with "; " in the order applied by add_processing_level(), so the attribute doubles as the per-variable procedure sequence. Comma is unusable as a separator — RANGES_FLAGGED contains one.

ctdcast.processors.history.add_processing_level(attrs: MutableMapping[str, object], value: str) → None[source]

Append a table-3 processing_level value to attrs, idempotently.

The attribute is an ordered set joined with "; ": value is appended only if it is not already present, so re-running a stage — or two stages that apply the same procedure (stage-2 soak/deck and stage-3 gross-range both flag) — never accumulates a duplicate. Order of first application is preserved, so the attribute reads as the procedure sequence.

Parameters:

  • attrs – A variable’s attribute mapping (ds[var].attrs), mutated in place.

  • value – One of the PL_* table-3 strings.

ctdcast.processors.history.append_history(attrs: MutableMapping[str, object], note: str, *, stage: str, version: str = '0.4.1', producer: str = 'ctdcast', timestamp: str | None = None, prepend: bool = False) → None[source]

Append a stamped history line to attrs in place.

Parameters:

  • attrs – The attribute mapping to extend — an xarray ds.attrs or the plain dict a builder assembles before constructing its Dataset. Mutated in place: the existing history (if any) is preserved and the new line is appended after a newline.

  • note – The human-readable record of the operation, including the parameters it used (e.g. "gross_range: ctd_salinity_1:[2.0,42.0]").

  • stage – The stage token that did the work — "stage1", "stage2", "stage3", "profiles", "ladcp_profiles" for ctdcast’s own stages, or a Sea-Bird module name ("celltm", "binavg", …) for an upstream step.

  • version – The version to stamp; defaults to the installed ctdcast package version.

  • producer – Who did the work — "ctdcast" by default. An upstream Sea-Bird step passes "SBE Data Processing" so the line reads as Sea-Bird’s, not ctdcast’s.

  • timestamp – The stamp to use. None (the default) uses the current ISO-8601 UTC time. A Sea-Bird step passes its own verbatim timestamp, kept as-is — no Z is appended, because it comes from a processing workstation whose offset is unknown and a different clock again from the deck unit.

  • prepend – Insert the line at the front of history instead of the end. Used for an upstream step (a Sea-Bird module) that predates the reader’s own line, so the record stays oldest-first; the default appends.

The processing steps data_processing.steps may list: one table, used by stage 3 and the checks.

Each Step names a Sea-Bird module, says whether stage 3 applies it yet, how it is applied, and how its parameters are checked before any cast is processed. STEPS is the single list: adding a step is one row here; stage 3, iter_steps() and validate_data_processing() all read it.

A step listed in the config but not yet applied is refused unless the config says allow_unapplied: true beside steps: the steps after it would otherwise run on data the config meant to be changed first, and the stage-3 file would look complete. With the switch, the step is skipped, named in a warning, in history and in the file’s data_processing_steps attribute.

allowed only in data_processing.products.

Stage-3 editing at the native scan rate: Sea-Bird’s Wild Edit and Loop Edit.

Wild Edit marks values that sit far from the rest of their block of scans, as SBE Data Processing’s module of the same name does: in each block of scans_per_block scans, the values beyond pass1_nstd standard deviations of the block mean are set aside, the mean and standard deviation are recomputed from what is left, and a value is marked when it lies beyond pass2_nstd of those and farther than mindelta from the mean. The last, partial block is judged against the last full scans_per_block scans of the cast.

Sea-Bird replaces a marked value with its bad flag; ctdcast keeps the value and sets {var}_qc to QARTOD 4 (fail), so nothing is lost and the edit is visible in the file. The parameters and the number of values marked are recorded on each variable and in history.

The marking is seabirdscientific.processing.wild_edit()’s; ctdcast turns its bad-flag values into _qc flags and keeps the data.

Where it appears to differ from SBE Data Processing (Sea-Bird’s Windows program). On a block where a channel sits at one or two A/D levels (an SBE 43 voltage, altimeter or fluorescence near the surface), the standard deviation left after the first pass is about zero. With mindelta 0 the Windows program then marks every value in the block; seabirdscientific marks only the values off the block’s main level. On OdB cast 050 every value ctdcast marked was also marked in the cruise’s CNV, which marked 5–10 times more on those channels, in whole blocks. The cause is inferred from the output, not from the Windows program’s source. A mindelta of a few A/D steps on such channels avoids both.

Loop Edit marks whole scans where the package went up on the downcast (or down on the upcast), moved slower than min_velocity, or was still in the surface soak, with seabirdscientific.processing.loop_edit(). ctdcast keeps every value: the marks go into loop_edit_flag and QARTOD 4 in each variable’s _qc, and later steps (Wild Edit and Window Filter with exclude_flagged, Bin Average) leave the marked scans out.

Deck pressure. With deck_pressure: true, seabirdscientific offsets the soak window by the first scan’s depth. On OdB casts 011, 017 and 050, whose CNV headers say useDeckPress = 1, SBE Data Processing’s marks match no offset instead (the recordings start with the package already in the water, 1.8–7.5 dbar): with the first-scan offset the soak runs 90–800 scans longer, with none the two agree except at 20–40 single scans at the speed threshold. deck_pressure also takes a number, the deck pressure in dbar, so deck_pressure: 0 reproduces those CNVs.

Configuration, a step in data_processing.steps:

- wildedit:
    pass1_nstd: 2.0
    pass2_nstd: 20.0
    mindelta: 0.0
    scans_per_block: 100
    exclude_flagged: true    # leave scans an earlier Loop Edit marked out of the statistics
    variables: [pressure, ctd_temperature_1, conductivity_1]
- loopedit:
    min_velocity: 0.25         # dbar/s; or mean_speed_percent: 20 with window_seconds: 300
    surface_soak: {min_depth: 5.0, max_depth: 20.0, deck_pressure: true}   # or false
    exclude_flagged: true
ctdcast.processors.editing.DEFAULT_WILD_EDIT_VARIABLES = ('pressure', 'ctd_temperature_1', 'ctd_temperature_2', 'conductivity_1', 'conductivity_2', 'oxygen_raw_1', 'oxygen_raw_2')

Stage-3 filters at the native scan rate: Sea-Bird’s Filter and Window Filter.

  • Filter (filter step): Sea-Bird’s low-pass filter, a single-pole filter run forward and backward so it adds no lag, with one time constant (SBE Data Processing manual, Filter). Sea-Bird’s module applies two time constants, A and B, to two lists of variables in one run; in data_processing.steps that is two filter entries. Applied with seabirdscientific.processing.low_pass_filter().

  • Window Filter (window_filter step): a boxcar, cosine, triangle, gaussian or median window of width scans, with seabirdscientific.processing.window_filter().

Both change values; the parameters are recorded on each variable (filters, one entry per filter, in order) and in history. Values an earlier Wild Edit marked are left out of the filter, as SBE Data Processing leaves out its bad flags: the filter runs across them on values interpolated from their neighbours, and the marked values themselves are kept as they were. On OdB cast 050, Filter on .hex data matches the cruise’s CNV to its rounding for pressure (0.15 s) and fluorescence (0.03 s).

Configuration, steps in data_processing.steps:

- filter: {time_constant: 0.15, variables: [pressure]}
- window_filter: {type: median, width: 10, variables: [pressure, ctd_fluor],
                  exclude_flagged: true}     # gaussian also takes half_width, offset

Products: files made from the stage-3 file by further steps, such as a 1 dbar downcast.

Sea-Bird processing usually runs one sequence of steps and then branches: the same corrected scans become a 1 s time series, a 1 dbar downcast and a 1 dbar upcast, each with its own Loop Edit and Bin Average. data_processing.products lists these branches; each has a name and its own steps, run on the stage-3 data (every scan, already through data_processing.steps):

data_processing:
  steps: [...]                       # the stage-3 file
  products:
    - name: 1dbar_down
      steps:
        - split: down
        - loopedit: {min_velocity: 0.25}
        - binavg: {bin: decibars, size: 1}
    - name: 1sec
      steps:
        - binavg: {bin: seconds, size: 1}

A product may use any step; split and binavg are product-only, because the stage-3 file keeps every scan, and binavg comes last. Each product is written to <ctd_root>/products/<name>/<cast>_<name>.nc; the stage-3 file is unchanged.

Bin Average (binavg) uses seabirdscientific.processing.bin_average(). Bins are decibars (on pressure), seconds (from the first scan) or scans. A value is left out of its bin when its _qc is 4 (fail) or 9 (missing) — so Wild Edit’s marks, stage 2’s soak and deck flags and a failed gross-range test leave out that one value, not its whole scan — and, with exclude_flagged, the scans Loop Edit marked are left out entirely, as SBE Data Processing does. Salinity is re-derived from the binned conductivity, temperature and pressure. Bins of a pressure product run down then up unless a split chose one leg.

Stage-3 corrections at the native scan rate: alignment, cell thermal mass, and SBE 43 oxygen.

These are the Sea-Bird processing steps that only make sense on unbinned, unfiltered data at the instrument’s own scan rate (24 Hz on a 911plus), applied with Sea-Bird’s seabirdscientific toolkit:

  • alignment (processing.align_ctd): advance conductivity, or an SBE 43 voltage, relative to pressure by a configured number of seconds;

  • cell thermal mass (processing.cell_thermal_mass): correct conductivity for the heat the conductivity cell stores, from the temperature of the same line;

  • oxygen (conversion.convert_sbe43_oxygen): derive ctd_oxygen from the aligned SBE 43 voltage and the corrected temperature, salinity and pressure of its line, with the tau and hysteresis corrections of Sea-Bird Application Note 64-3.

Where this diverges from seabirdscientific (3.1.1). The tau and hysteresis corrections are computed here (sbe43_dvdt(), sbe43_hysteresis(), sbe43_tau_term()) and folded into the voltage, and convert_sbe43_oxygen is then called with both of its corrections off. Two reasons: speed (seabirdscientific fits a regression per scan for dV/dt, about 11 s on a 3000 dbar cast; the same least-squares slope as a convolution agrees to 1e-12 V/s in milliseconds), and the hysteresis recursion (seabirdscientific feeds the corrected previous voltage where Application Note 64-3 uses the uncorrected one; the two differ by a few µmol/kg at depth). The divergence is recorded on every derived variable (oxygen_hysteresis_method) and should be removed once seabirdscientific matches Application Note 64-3: call convert_sbe43_oxygen with apply_tau_correction and apply_hysteresis_correction on again, and drop the three functions.

Every step records its parameters on the variable it changed and in history, so the correction is reconstructable from the output file alone. A step that cannot apply to a cast (the data is binned, or Sea-Bird already applied the same step) is skipped with a warning and a history note; the cast’s other stage-3 steps still run.

Configuration (data_processing:, see ctdcast.config.layout): alignctd and celltm are steps in data_processing.steps, each entry a bare value or a default and/or ranges (casts + value) declaration; the oxygen window and the per-sensor conductivity slope and offset sit beside the steps:

data_processing:
  slope_offset:                # per conductivity sensor: C' = slope * C + offset
    conductivity_1: {slope: 1.0000452, offset: 0.0}
  oxygen:
    tau_window_seconds: 2.0    # window for the SBE 43 tau correction's dV/dt
  steps:
    - alignctd:                # seconds; + advances the variable relative to pressure
        conductivity: 0.0
        oxygen: 3.0
        conductivity_2: {ranges: [{casts: [[30, 45]], value: 0.021}]}
    - celltm:                  # alpha and tau (1/beta, seconds); conductivity only
        conductivity: {alpha: 0.03, tau: 7.0}

ctdcast.processors.corrections.cell_thermal_mass(conductivity_mS_cm: ndarray, temperature: ndarray, alpha: float, tau_seconds: float, interval_seconds: float) → ndarray[source]

Correct conductivity for cell thermal mass with seabirdscientific’s cell_thermal_mass.

seabirdscientific’s filter works in S/m (its 0.1 × (1 + 0.006 (T − 20)) term is S/m per °C), so conductivity is converted from mS/cm to S/m, corrected, and converted back.

Parameters:

  • conductivity_mS_cm (numpy.ndarray) – Conductivity in mS/cm at the native scan rate.

  • temperature (numpy.ndarray) – Temperature (°C, ITS-90) of the same line; must be finite throughout, since the recursive filter would carry a NaN to every later scan.

  • alpha (float) – Thermal anomaly amplitude.

  • tau_seconds (float) – Thermal anomaly time constant (1/beta), in seconds.

  • interval_seconds (float) – Time between scans.

Returns:

Corrected conductivity in mS/cm (float64).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – If the temperature has non-finite values, or alpha < 0 or tau <= 0. Alpha = 0 returns the conductivity unchanged.

ctdcast.processors.corrections.derive_oxygen(ds: Dataset, cruise_cfg: dict | None = None, *, cast_label: str = '?', marked: dict[str, ndarray] | None = None) → tuple[Dataset, list[str]][source]

Derive ctd_oxygen from each SBE 43 voltage, as Sea-Bird’s Data Conversion does.

For each oxygen_raw_<N> with no converted oxygen beside it (a CNV’s own ctd_oxygen is never re-derived), oxygen in µmol/kg is computed with convert_sbe43_oxygen from the (aligned) voltage, the temperature, practical salinity and pressure of line N (line 1 if the cast has no line N), and the sensor’s coefficients from the .xmlcon in raw_metadata, with the tau and hysteresis corrections on (Sea-Bird Application Note 64-3). One sensor gives plain ctd_oxygen; two give ctd_oxygen_1/_2.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – A stage-3 dataset after alignment, CTM and salinity.

  • cruise_cfg (dict or None) – The data_processing: block; oxygen.tau_window_seconds sets the tau-correction window.

  • cast_label (str, optional) – How the cast is named in warnings.

  • marked (dict of str to numpy.ndarray, optional) – {variable: mask} of values an earlier Wild Edit marked. The tau and hysteresis corrections step scan to scan, so a marked voltage, temperature, conductivity or pressure would spread into the neighbouring oxygen; each is replaced by interpolation from its unmarked neighbours for the conversion, and the oxygen at those scans is flagged 4.

Returns:

A new dataset and the names of the variables written.

Return type:

tuple of (xarray.Dataset, list of str)

ctdcast.processors.corrections.native_interval(ds: Dataset) → tuple[float | None, str | None][source]

Return the scan interval to correct ds with, or why it cannot be corrected.

Alignment, cell thermal mass and the SBE 43 tau correction act scan by scan; on binned or averaged data they would be wrong. All of these must hold: sample_interval_seconds equals the instrument’s native interval (911plus: 1/24 s), the deck unit averaged no scans, and the Sea-Bird chain has no binavg.

The interval returned is the instrument’s exact native interval (911plus: 1/24 s), not the recorded one: a CNV writes it rounded (seconds: 0.0416667), and the rounded value makes seabirdscientific’s time axis one sample long for some cast lengths. A stage file written before stage 1 recorded the interval falls back to the CNV header’s # interval line.

Parameters:

ds (xarray.Dataset) – A stage-2 or stage-3 per-cast dataset.

Returns:

(interval_seconds, None) at the native rate, else (None, reason).

Return type:

tuple of (float or None, str or None)

ctdcast.processors.corrections.sbe43_dvdt(volts: ndarray, window_seconds: float, interval: float) → ndarray[source]

Return dV/dt for the SBE 43 tau correction: a least-squares slope over a centred window.

The same slope seabirdscientific’s convert_sbe43_oxygen fits scan by scan, as one convolution. floor(window / 2 / interval) scans each side; the scans within that many of either end get 0, as in seabirdscientific.

Parameters:

  • volts (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage at the native scan rate, without gaps.

  • window_seconds (float) – Width of the fitting window, in seconds.

  • interval (float) – Time between scans, in seconds.

Returns:

dV/dt in V/s, the same length as volts.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

ctdcast.processors.corrections.sbe43_hysteresis(volts: ndarray, pressure: ndarray, coefs: Oxygen43Coefficients, interval: float) → ndarray[source]

Return SBE 43 voltage corrected for hysteresis, as Sea-Bird Application Note 64-3 gives it.

Oxnew(i) = (Ox(i) + Oxnew(i-1)·C·D − Ox(i-1)·C) / D with Ox = V + Voffset, D = 1 + H1·(exp(P/H2) − 1) and C = exp(−interval/H3); Ox(i-1) is the uncorrected previous value. Written as y(i) = C·y(i-1) + (x(i) − C·x(i-1))/D(i), a first-order recursive filter.

Parameters:

  • volts (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage, without gaps.

  • pressure (numpy.ndarray) – Pressure (dbar), same length.

  • coefs (seabirdscientific.cal_coefficients.Oxygen43Coefficients) – The sensor’s calibration (h1, h2, h3, v_offset).

  • interval (float) – Time between scans, in seconds.

Returns:

Corrected voltage (V), the same length; the first scan is unchanged.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

ctdcast.processors.corrections.sbe43_oxygen(volts: ndarray, temperature: ndarray, pressure: ndarray, salinity: ndarray, coefs: Oxygen43Coefficients, window_seconds: float, interval: float) → ndarray[source]

Return SBE 43 oxygen (µmol/kg) with the tau and Application Note 64-3 hysteresis corrections.

dV/dt comes from the uncorrected voltage and hysteresis acts on the voltage, as in seabirdscientific; the corrected voltage plus the tau term then goes through convert_sbe43_oxygen with its own corrections off.

Parameters:

  • volts (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage, ITS-90 temperature (°C), pressure (dbar) and practical salinity of one unbroken run of finite scans.

  • temperature (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage, ITS-90 temperature (°C), pressure (dbar) and practical salinity of one unbroken run of finite scans.

  • pressure (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage, ITS-90 temperature (°C), pressure (dbar) and practical salinity of one unbroken run of finite scans.

  • salinity (numpy.ndarray) – SBE 43 voltage, ITS-90 temperature (°C), pressure (dbar) and practical salinity of one unbroken run of finite scans.

  • coefs (seabirdscientific.cal_coefficients.Oxygen43Coefficients) – The sensor’s calibration.

  • window_seconds (float) – The tau correction’s dV/dt window, in seconds.

  • interval (float) – Time between scans, in seconds.

Returns:

Oxygen in µmol/kg.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

ctdcast.processors.corrections.sbe43_tau_term(dvdt: ndarray, temperature: ndarray, pressure: ndarray, coefs: Oxygen43Coefficients) → ndarray[source]

Return the tau correction in volts: tau20·exp(D1·P + D2·(T − 20))·dV/dt.

Added to the voltage, it gives what seabirdscientific’s equation does with its tau term.

Returns:

The term, in volts.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

fit is ctdcast fit: it scores every native-rate stage-2 cast with fits, writes the cost surfaces to fits.nc, and turns them into the cruise summary and the suggested data_processing: block.

ctdcast fit: fit alignment and cell thermal mass over a cruise and record the results.

Reads every stage-2 cast at its native scan rate, scores each conductivity line with the cost functions in ctdcast.analysis.fits, and writes the per-cast cost surfaces to <ctd_root>/fits.nc. The cruise and per-block averages are not stored — summarise() computes them from the per-cast costs at report time. The report draws the corrections page from that file. Nothing here changes a stage file: the values reach stage 3 only through the config.

Two passes: alignment first, over every cast; then cell thermal mass on conductivity advanced by the cruise’s fitted (downcast) alignment for that line, because a misaligned line fits the wrong (alpha, tau).

The file fit writes and report reads, under the CTD root.

Stage layout

Where each stage’s files live and how a file’s stage is read from its name.

On-disk stage layout: per-stage paths and best-available cast-file discovery.

The single source of truth for the stage-file naming, so nothing elsewhere hard-codes _stageN or stageN/. Each processing stage writes its own per-cast netCDF under a stage subdirectory of one instrument root, with the stage carried in the filename as well as the path:

<root>/stage1/<cast_stem>_stage1.nc
<root>/stage2/<cast_stem>_stage2.nc
<root>/stage3/<cast_stem>_stage3.nc

The subdirectory bounds each directory’s file count by cast count rather than cast count times stages; the filename suffix means a file copied out of its directory is still identifiable and still parses. parse_stage() reads the stage off the filename and does not trust the parent directory, so the two can disagree (the filename wins, with a warning) without losing the file.

The cast stages here mirror the "cast"-scope entries of ctdcast.processors.STAGES (the pipeline registry); the two are tied by a consistency test rather than derived from each other, because the registry imports the stage modules that import this one — deriving would be an import cycle.

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.PRODUCT_SUFFIX = 'profiles.nc'

Filename suffix of the compiled gridded products (profiles.nc, ladcp_profiles.nc) that sit at the stage root beside the stage directories.

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.STAGES: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 2, 3)

The per-cast stages that write stage files, in ascending order.

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.STAGE_DIRS: dict[int, str] = {1: 'stage1', 2: 'stage2', 3: 'stage3'}

Subdirectory under the instrument root that holds each stage’s files. This is the one hand-maintained map; the suffixes and the stage tuple derive from it, so adding a stage (e.g. a future hex→CNV stage 0) is a single line here.

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.STAGE_SUFFIXES: dict[int, str] = {1: '_stage1', 2: '_stage2', 3: '_stage3'}

Filename suffix (before .nc) carried by each stage’s per-cast file. The stage’s directory name and filename suffix are the same token by construction, matching the sibling oceanarray package’s “stage name doubles as the suffix”.

Precedence is stage 3, then stage 2, then stage 1 — the one place this rule lives.

  • cast_stem (str) – The cast’s base stem, without any stage suffix.

Returns:

The best-available per-cast file, or None when no stage file exists.

Return type:

Path or None

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.group_by_cast(root: Path | str) → dict[tuple[int, str], dict[int, Path]][source]

Map each cast identity to the stage files present for it.

Walks root/stage*/ and groups every recognised stage file by its cast identity (cast_num, cast_suffix) — so a plain cast NNN and its lettered sibling NNNb are distinct keys. Files whose name carries no stage suffix or no cast number are skipped.

A suffix-less *.nc directly under the root (the old flat nc_dir layout, and the committed test fixtures) is folded in as stage 1, unless a nested stage1/…_stage1.nc already exists for that cast — the nested file wins. Compiled products such as profiles.nc carry no cast number and are skipped automatically.

Parameters:

root (Path or str) – The instrument stage root.

Returns:

{(cast_num, cast_suffix): {stage: path}}.

Return type:

dict

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.is_product_name(name: Path | str) → bool[source]

Return whether name is a compiled-product file, not a per-cast file.

Compiled products (…profiles.nc) live at the stage root; they are terminal gridded artefacts, not casts, and must never be folded into cast discovery — even when the name carries a cruise number (e.g. msm_142_profiles.nc), which would otherwise parse as cast 142.

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.is_up_to_date(target: Path | str, sources: Iterable[Path]) → bool[source]

Return whether target exists and is newer than every source in sources.

The one skip/re-run test for a derived file (a stage output or a compiled product): skip only when the output already exists and no input has been rewritten since (by mtime). This is what makes a forced re-run of an earlier step propagate — process --stage 1 --only 42 --force followed by a plain process --stage 2 3 profiles regenerates cast 42 downstream instead of silently skipping because a stale output happened to exist. A missing source is ignored (it cannot make the target stale).

ctdcast.processors.stage_layout.matches_tags(cast_id: tuple[int, str], tags: set[str]) → bool[source]

Return whether cast_id is selected by any zero-padded cast tag.

Matches on the parsed cast identity, not a filename substring — so a cruise or leg number in the stem cannot be mistaken for the cast number (the bug in the old tag in stem rule), and a lettered sibling 004b is selected by its own tag ("004b") or by the bare number ("004").

Parameters:

  • cast_id (tuple of (int, str)) – The (cast_num, cast_suffix) identity from group_by_cast().

  • tags (set of str) – Zero-padded cast tags (e.g. {"042", "004b"}), as the CLI produces from --only.

Returns:

True if any tag names this cast.

Return type:

bool

The one place the best-available precedence lives for every consumer (the report, build_profiles, the LADCP compile). best_path is the highest-stage file present (3 > 2 > 1); source_stage is that stage, or 0 when the best file is a flat/suffix-less file that does not state its own stage (the compatibility shim only assumes stage 1, so 0 = “unknown, guessed stage 1” stays distinct from a stated stage 1).

LADCP processing: LDEO .mat → per-cast netCDF → compiled ladcp_profiles.nc.

Mirrors the CTD pipeline (stage1 convert_cast → build_profiles): convert_ladcp_cast() translates one LDEO .mat solution to a per-cast ladcp_<cast_id>.nc on the native 10 m depth grid, with storage dtypes reduced for file size; the compiler (added in build_ladcp_profiles()) concatenates those per-cast files onto a common depth axis.

ctdcast.processors.ladcp.build_ladcp_profiles(ladcp_nc_dir: Path, ladcp_profiles_path: Path, *, force: bool = False, cruise_info: dict | None = None) → bool[source]

Compile per-cast ladcp_*.nc into ladcp_profiles.nc.

The LADCP parallel of ctdcast.processors.profiles.build_profiles(). Because each cast is already on a uniform 10 m grid, this is a common-axis alignment (not a regrid): every profile is reindexed onto the deepest cast’s depth axis (NaN below its own bottom) and stacked on a new N_PROF dimension. Per-cast scalars become N_PROF vectors; cruise-common provenance is kept in attrs, per-cast-varying provenance is already stored as variables. Returns True if written, False when there is nothing to compile.

Skips when ladcp_profiles.nc already exists and is newer than every per-cast source file (same source-mtime rule as the CTD compiler and the processing stages); force rebuilds regardless.

cruise_info (the config cruise_info: block) supplies discovery metadata, people, embargo, and the ship/date for the EXPOCODE coordinate. Coverage bounds (lat/lon from the per-cast positions, vertical from the depth axis in metres) and the creation time are computed from the data.

ctdcast.processors.ladcp.run_convert(ladcp_dir: Path, ladcp_nc_dir: Path, *, force: bool = False, dry_run: bool = False, cast_tags: set[str] | None = None, cruise_info: dict | None = None, **kw: object) → int[source]

Convert every LADCP .mat in ladcp_dir to a per-cast netCDF.

The LADCP parallel of ctdcast.processors.stage1.run(): discovers the .mat files, derives each cast’s identity from its filename, and writes ladcp_nc_dir/stage1/ladcp_<cast_id>_stage1.nc. LADCP has a single processing stage, so its stage-1 file is its per-cast product. Files with no cast number in the stem are skipped. Returns the number of files written (0 for dry_run). cruise_info is stamped as cruise identity on each file.

Canonicalise variable units at each processing boundary.

The units knowledge — which spelling is canonical per quantity, which reader spellings convert to it and with what factor — is the shared family data in ctdcast.reports._vendored.units_tables, read through ctdcast.reports._vendored.units.resolve_units(); ctdcast’s view of it, with its own additions, is ctdcast.config.unit_tables.TABLES. This module holds only the transform that applies it, to_canonical_units() — a loop over resolve_units run at the netCDF write boundary (every stage persists through the writer, so each stage’s output is canonicalised). Every written file carries one canonical spelling per quantity, a factor ≠ 1 spelling has its values converted, and an unrecognised spelling stops the run loudly rather than being silently overwritten.

The display spelling (mS cm-1 → mS/cm) is a separate concern, derived from the canonical string by ctdcast.config.unit_tables.unit_label(); it is never stored.

exception ctdcast.processors.units.UnitsError[source]

A units string cannot be related to a canonical spelling.

Raised by resolve_units() for a present spelling that is not a recognised member of its canonical’s alias group, and by merge_tables() for an alias factor that disagrees with the base. A dedicated ValueError subclass so a caller can catch this specifically without swallowing unrelated ValueError exceptions.

ctdcast.processors.units.to_canonical_units(ds: xr.Dataset, *, tables: Tables = Tables(canonical={'sea_water_pressure': 'dbar', 'latitude': 'degrees_north', 'longitude': 'degrees_east', 'sea_water_temperature': 'degree_Celsius', 'sea_water_conservative_temperature': 'degree_Celsius', 'sea_water_electrical_conductivity': 'mS cm-1', 'sea_water_practical_salinity': '1', 'sea_water_absolute_salinity': 'g kg-1', 'moles_of_oxygen_per_unit_mass_in_sea_water': 'umol kg-1', 'mass_concentration_of_chlorophyll_in_sea_water': 'mg m-3', 'sea_water_turbidity': '1', 'altitude_of_sea_floor': 'm', 'sea_water_sigma_theta': 'kg m-3', 'eastward_sea_water_velocity': 'm s-1', 'northward_sea_water_velocity': 'm s-1', 'square_of_brunt_vaisala_frequency_in_sea_water': 'rad2 s-2'}, aliases={'degree_Celsius': {'degC': 1.0, 'degrees_C': 1.0, 'Degrees C': 1.0, '°C': 1.0, 'ITS-90, deg C': 1.0}, 'mS cm-1': {'mS/cm': 1.0, 'S/m': 10.0}, 'm': {'meters': 1.0}, 'dbar': {'db': 1.0}, 'm s-1': {'m/s': 1.0}, 'umol kg-1': {'umol/kg': 1.0, 'µmol/kg': 1.0}, 'kg m-3': {'kg/m³': 1.0}, 'g kg-1': {'g/kg': 1.0}, 'mg m-3': {'mg/m^3': 1.0}, 'percent': {'% saturation': 1.0}, 'degrees_north': {'degree_north': 1.0, 'degree_N': 1.0, 'degrees_N': 1.0, 'degreeN': 1.0, 'degreesN': 1.0}, 'degrees_east': {'degree_east': 1.0, 'degree_E': 1.0, 'degrees_E': 1.0, 'degreeE': 1.0, 'degreesE': 1.0}, 'degree': {'degrees': 1.0, '°': 1.0}, 'V': {'volts': 1.0}, 's': {'seconds': 1.0}}, scoped={'sea_water_practical_salinity': {'PSU': 1.0}, 'sea_water_turbidity': {'NTU': 1.0}, 'latitude': {'deg': 1.0}, 'longitude': {'deg': 1.0}}, labels={'degree_Celsius': '°C', 'degrees_north': '°N', 'degrees_east': '°E', 'percent': '%', 'degree': '°'}, labels_by_standard_name={'sea_water_turbidity': 'NTU', 'sea_water_practical_salinity': 'PSU'}, tokens={'umol': 'µmol'}), registry: dict[str, str] | None = None, log_fn: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, stage: int | str | None = None) → xr.Dataset[source]

Rewrite each registered variable’s units to its canonical spelling.

The canonical for a variable is its registry units when the variable is registered (known by name, which works before the writer stamps standard_name on the dataset), else the canonical for its CF standard_name. The current units string is resolved against that canonical’s accepted group (the canonical ×1 plus the family aliases plus the scoped spellings for the quantity); a factor ≠ 1 match multiplies the values and drops any stale integer packing, a pure spelling rewrite leaves the values untouched. The conversion is not stamped on the variable — a factor ≠ 1 is reported through log_fn at the boundary. Temperature variables additionally get the CF-1.11 units_metadata = "temperature: on_scale".

A registered variable with no units attribute has its canonical filled from the registry (ctdcast derives composites and carries channels whose units are supplied at the write boundary, not by the reader) — a fill, not a conversion. The pass is idempotent — a variable already carrying its canonical string is left unchanged — so it runs at every write without double-converting (stage 2/3 re-read an already-canonical stage-1 file). Unregistered engineering variables (no registry entry and no matching standard_name) are left untouched.

Parameters:

  • ds (xarray.Dataset) – Dataset to canonicalise in place (also returned).

  • tables (Tables, optional) – The units view to resolve against; defaults to ctdcast.config.unit_tables.TABLES.

  • registry (dict of str to str, optional) – {variable name: standard_name} map; defaults to ctdcast.config.unit_tables.registry_standard_names(). Used to find a variable’s standard_name (for the scoped spellings) before the writer stamps it on the dataset.

  • log_fn (callable, optional) – Called with one message per variable whose units string changed.

  • stage (int or str, optional) – Processing stage, used only to annotate the log and error messages.

Returns:

The same dataset, with canonical units on every registered variable.

Return type:

xarray.Dataset

Raises:

UnitsError – If a registered variable carries a units string that is present but is not a recognised spelling of its canonical. The pass never guesses or silently passes an unknown unit through; a missing units attribute is filled (see above), not raised.

Reader for LDEO IXv14 LADCP .mat files.

Locates the .mat file for a cast (find_ladcp_file()), loads it with a single set of scipy.io.loadmat options (read_ladcp()), and maps the result struct to a single-cast xarray.Dataset on the native 10 m depth grid (read_ladcp_cast()). The .mat is the LDEO IX velocity solution; its ~50 fields are mapped to the compiled-dataset schema.

ctdcast.readers.ladcp.MatField

A field read from a scipy.io.loadmat mat-struct — an ndarray, a mat_struct, or a scalar, depending on how MATLAB stored it. Named once here so the struct accessors below read field: MatField with no per-signature noqa, the explanation travels into the docs, and a future narrowing happens in one place.

ctdcast.readers.ladcp.find_ladcp_file(ladcp_dir: Path, cast_num: int, cast_suffix: str = '', ladcp_pattern: str | None = None) → Path | None[source]

Return the .mat file for cast_num in ladcp_dir, or None if absent.

If ladcp_pattern is given (e.g. "msm_142_1_*.mat"), the * wildcard is replaced with the zero-padded cast number (and optional suffix) and that name is tried first. Falls back to standard names (NNN.mat, NNNb.mat) then a *_NNN.mat glob for cruise-prefixed filenames. The first glob match (lexicographic) is returned when multiple files match.

ctdcast.readers.ladcp.read_ladcp(path: Path | str) → dict[str, Any][source]

Load an LDEO IXv14 LADCP .mat file.

Uses squeeze_me=True and struct_as_record=False so the LADCP result struct is reachable as read_ladcp(path)["dr"] with attribute access.

ctdcast.readers.ladcp.read_ladcp_cast(path: Path | str, *, cast_num: int, cast_suffix: str = '') → Dataset[source]

Map an LDEO LADCP .mat to a single-cast Dataset on the native 10 m grid.

Returns a Dataset with dimension depth (uniform 10 m, positive down), an auxiliary pressure(depth) coordinate (dbar, the bridge to profiles.nc), the inverse (u/v) and shear (u_shear/v_shear/w_shear) velocity solutions, per-instrument down/up-looker profiles, per-cast scalars (barotropic, bottom-track, position, instrument_config), and the LADCP processing provenance as global attributes. Velocity carries the CF eastward/northward/error_sea_water_velocity standard names.

Reader for per-cast sensor metadata written by seasenselib.

Parses the raw_metadata global attribute (a JSON blob) into a list of sensor descriptors for the cast page.

ctdcast.readers.metadata.parse_sensor_channels(ds: Dataset) → list[dict][source]

Return one full descriptor per sensor channel in ds, from the raw header.

A thin reader over ctdcast.config.cnv_header.parse_sensor_block() (the single parser of the <Sensors> block, authoritative because seasenselib’s per-channel cnv_sensor_N dicts are lossy for some channels): it resolves the block comment to a canonical role and normalises the calibration_date. Free (unused) channels get role = None and an empty serial.

A cast read from a .hex has no <Sensors> block in its header; its sensors come from the .xmlcon carried in raw_metadata, rendered in the same record shape by ctdcast.readers.xmlcon.sensor_records().

Returns [] if raw_metadata carries neither a header sensor block nor an .xmlcon. Each dict has channel, element, sensor_id, serial, calibration_date (normalised), slope, offset and role (canonical role or None).

ctdcast.readers.metadata.parse_sensor_info(ds: Dataset) → list[dict[str, str]][source]

Extract sensor serial numbers and calibration dates from ds.

Parses the raw_metadata global attribute (a JSON string written by seasenselib) and returns one entry per sensor channel that has both a sensor_type and a serial_number.

Parameters:

ds – Per-cast Dataset as opened from a netCDF file.

Returns:

Each dict has keys sensor_type (human-readable label), serial_number, and calibration_date. Returns [] if raw_metadata is absent, unparseable, or contains no usable sensors.

Return type:

list[dict[str, str]]

ctdcast.readers.metadata.source_to_canonical(ds: Dataset, *, lower_keys: bool = False) → dict[str, str][source]

Reconstruct a reader’s {source_name: canonical_name} rename table from ds.

Reads each coordinate and data variable’s recorded source name (_SOURCE_NAME_ATTRS) and maps it to the variable’s canonical name, keeping only variables whose source name actually differs. This is the authoritative, per-cast rename the reader applied — more complete than the static CNV_ALIASES, which misses unit spellings such as c0mS/cm. lower_keys lower-cases the keys, for case-insensitive lookup against header channel names.

Reader for Sea-Bird SBE 911plus .hex files, on seabirdscientific directly.

A .hex holds one line of hexadecimal per scan at the instrument’s native rate (24 Hz on a 911plus), after a *-prefixed header that ends at *END*. Reading it takes the matching .xmlcon (ctdcast.readers.xmlcon) for the channel layout and the calibration coefficients.

What read_hex() returns, at the native rate and with nothing removed:

  • pressure, ctd_temperature_1/2, conductivity_1/2 in mS/cm, each with the .xmlcon Slope and Offset applied as Sea-Bird’s DatCnv does;

  • every voltage channel as raw volts (volt<N>_raw; an SBE 43 channel as oxygen_raw_<N>), plus the engineering value for each sensor seabirdscientific converts (fluorescence, turbidity, altimeter, beam transmission) and a quick-look SBE 43 oxygen;

  • the deck unit’s per-scan status bits and data-integrity counter;

  • time, latitude, longitude coordinates.

The time axis is built forward from the first scan: scan k is at T0 + k × interval. T0 is the header’s NMEA UTC (Time) (GPS time when acquisition started) when present and sane, else the header’s System UpLoad Time (the PC clock at the first scan), uncorrected and labelled as the System clock so the stage-2 clock correction can apply to it.

Check a .bl bottle log against the scan clock.

Each .bl line holds a bottle’s fire time (PC clock, whole seconds) and the scan range it covers. If the upload time is the first scan and scans are evenly spaced, every fire time equals upload_time + first_scan × interval to within a second. A wrong anchor or a file with dropped scans fails.

Reader for Sea-Bird .xmlcon instrument configuration files (SBE 911plus).

An .xmlcon is the configuration Seasave writes beside each .hex: the instrument settings (which channels are suppressed, what the deck unit appends to each scan) and one <Sensor index=…> element per channel, holding the sensor’s serial number, calibration date and coefficients.

This module turns it into three things:

  • XmlconInstrument, the parsed settings and sensors;

  • seabirdscientific coefficient objects for the sensors ctdcast converts at stage 1 (temperature, conductivity, Digiquartz pressure, SBE 43 oxygen, ECO, altimeter, C-Star);

  • sensor records shaped exactly like ctdcast.config.cnv_header.parse_sensor_block()’s, so the per-cast sensor catalog is built by the same code for a .hex cast as for a .cnv one.

The <sensor> block a CNV header embeds is the same XML as the .xmlcon’s <Sensor> element, wrapped differently and preceded by a comment naming the channel and its quantity (<!-- Frequency 3, Temperature, 2 -->). sensor_records() rebuilds that wrapping, so raw_block reads the same whichever file the sensor came from.

Original author: Joel Bracamontes Ramirez, ctdproc (parsers.load_xmlcon), whose approach this follows: walk the <Sensor> elements in order, tell primary from secondary by the order of repeated sensor types, and build seabirdscientific coefficient objects. Rewritten for ctdcast.

Writers

CF-compliant netCDF writer for per-cast Datasets.

Augments the variable attributes produced by seasenselib with proper CF metadata from ctdcast.config.parameters.VARIABLES and writes QARTOD flag variables with the CF flag_values / flag_meanings convention. Writes atomically via a .nc.tmp intermediary.

ctdcast.writers.netcdf.write(ds: Dataset, path: Path, *, encoding: dict | None = None) → None[source]

Write ds to path with CF-1.13 attributes and QARTOD flag metadata.

Each registered variable’s units is first canonicalised to its CF spelling by ctdcast.processors.units.to_canonical_units() (which raises UnitsError on a present unrecognised spelling — the write is aborted, nothing is left on disk — and fills a missing units attribute from the registry). Then, for each variable present in both ds and VARIABLES — including coordinates such as latitude/longitude — applies long_name, standard_name, and comment (when defined). For each {var}_qc variable, generates complete CF flag attributes. Sets Conventions = "CF-1.13" unless the caller already declared one (a richer value such as "CF-1.13, ACDD-1.3" is preserved).

Writes atomically: writes to path.with_suffix(".nc.tmp") then replaces path so a failed write never leaves a partial file.

Every numeric variable with at least one dimension (coordinates included) is written with lossless zlib compression at level 4. The shuffle filter is applied to all of them except float64, where it was measured to enlarge ctdcast’s science columns. Compression is transparent on read and changes no stored values; a caller-supplied encoding for a variable is left untouched.

Parameters:

  • ds – Dataset to write (per-cast, dim=time, or profiles N_PROF×pressure).

  • path – Output netCDF path.

  • encoding – Optional xarray encoding dict passed through to to_netcdf.

Optimal storage-dtype selection for netCDF output.

Package-local data-saving utility — not part of the vendored report design system (which is about producing identical reports, not identical data). The two functions are ported from oceanarray and may diverge as ctdcast’s on-disk conventions require; keep them in sync by choice, not by vendoring discipline.

find_best_dtype() picks a variable’s storage dtype from its name and current dtype; cast_output_dtypes() applies that across a whole dataset (coordinates included) at the one write seam, shrinking file size (float64 → float32, int64 → int32, QC → int8) without touching time, position or provenance. widen_floats() is the reverse for a stage that reads a file to compute on it: storage is float32, arithmetic is float64.

ctdcast.writers.dtypes.cast_output_dtypes(ds: Dataset) → Dataset[source]

Cast every variable in ds to its optimal storage dtype.

Calls find_best_dtype() per variable, coordinates included, and rebuilds only those that change. Attributes are preserved. The input dataset is not modified. A float variable cast to an integer has NaN written as 9 (QARTOD missing) for a flag; ctdcast has no other float-to-integer case (serial numbers are text), and the 0 fill kept for one is oceanarray’s rule, copied unchanged.

Parameters:

ds (xr.Dataset) – Dataset to cast.

Returns:

New dataset with optimised dtypes, ready for NetCDF output.

Return type:

xr.Dataset

ctdcast.writers.dtypes.find_best_dtype(var_name: str, da: DataArray) → type[source]

Determine the optimal storage dtype for a variable.

Parameters:

  • var_name (str) – Variable name.

  • da (xr.DataArray) – Data array to inspect.

Returns:

Recommended numpy dtype.

Return type:

type

Notes

Rules applied in order:

  • String / datetime / timedelta / object variables: unchanged.

  • time as a word in the name: unchanged (preserve datetime64 / float encoding).

  • latitude / longitude (and lat / lon): float64, as everywhere in the family; they compress to almost nothing, so float32 would save no space.

  • *_qc suffix, or flag in a ctdcast name: int8. Sea-Bird’s own columns (sbe_) are never made integers: sbe_flag holds the bad flag -9.99e-29, which an integer would truncate to 0 (not flagged).

  • serial_number or serial: int32.

  • Integer input: downsize to int32 if stored as int64, else unchanged.

  • float64 input: float32 (about 10⁻⁷ relative, two to three orders of magnitude below the CTD sensors’ resolution).

  • Anything else: unchanged.

ctdcast.writers.dtypes.open_widened(path: Path, **open_kw: object) → Dataset[source]

Read a ctdcast file into memory, floats as float64, and close it.

The one way a stage reads a file it will compute on.

Parameters:

  • path (pathlib.Path) – The netCDF file.

  • **open_kw – Passed to xarray.open_dataset() (engine defaults to netcdf4).

Returns:

In memory, no open file handle, float32 variables as float64.

Return type:

xr.Dataset

ctdcast.writers.dtypes.widen_floats(ds: Dataset) → Dataset[source]

Return ds with every float32 variable as float64, for computation.

Files are stored as float32 (cast_output_dtypes()); a stage that reads one and computes on it (filters, recursive corrections, TEOS-10) does so in float64, so the float32 rounding happens once, at the write, and never compounds.

Parameters:

ds (xr.Dataset) – A dataset read from a ctdcast file.

Returns:

A new dataset, always (so a caller can change it freely); float32 variables (coordinates included) are float64. The input is not modified.

Return type:

xr.Dataset

The file defines two kinds of cast group – sections: (transects plotted against distance) and timeseries: (repeat stations plotted against time) – so groupings_yaml is the key, and ctd_groupings.yaml the conventional filename. section_yaml named only half of what the file does; it stays accepted, with a DeprecationWarning, until 0.5.0.

ctdcast.config.loader.load_display_config(cruise_cfg: dict[str, Any]) → dict[str, dict][source]

Return VARIABLES with cruise-level overrides applied.

Package defaults come from ctdcast.config.parameters.VARIABLES. Per-cruise overrides are read from cruise_cfg["display"]["variables"] (the display: block in the cruise config.yaml). Later keys win. Returns a new dict; nothing global is mutated, so the result can be recorded in the output file’s attributes for provenance.

Example cruise config override:

display:
  variables:
    temperature_1:
      vmin: 4
      vmax: 25

The single notice for the config-key spelling and the report() / init parameter spelling, so every entry point that still honours section_yaml emits the same DeprecationWarning naming the replacement and the removal version (0.5.0).

Frozen per-run report configuration, built once and threaded to the plotters.

ReportConfig replaces the runtime-mutable display globals that used to live on the plotting module (GEBCO_PATH, CLEAN_SPINES, the figsizes, the map bounds, and the colormap overrides). Building it once in ctdcast.report() and passing it down makes rendering order-independent and safe to parallelise — nothing mutates module state between figures.

DEFAULT_REPORT_CONFIG holds the defaults: the previous module-global values, except the overview-panel shape, which is 9 × 3 in (3:1).

ctdcast.config.report_config.DEFAULT_REPORT_CONFIG = ReportConfig(gebco_path=None, clean_spines=True, profile_figsize=(7.0, 10.0), overview_figsize=(9.0, 3.0), map_lat_min=None, map_lat_max=None, map_lon_min=None, map_lon_max=None, var_cmaps=mappingproxy({'ctd_temperature_1': 'RdYlBu_r', 'ctd_temperature_2': 'RdYlBu_r', 'ctd_temperature': 'RdYlBu_r', 'ctd_salinity_1': 'YlGnBu_r', 'ctd_salinity_2': 'YlGnBu_r', 'ctd_salinity': 'YlGnBu_r', 'ctd_oxygen_1': 'cmo.oxy', 'ctd_oxygen_2': 'cmo.oxy', 'ctd_oxygen': 'cmo.oxy', 'oxygen_saturation': 'BrBG', 'ctd_fluor': 'YlGn', 'ctd_turbidity': 'YlOrBr', 'conservative_temperature': 'RdYlBu_r', 'absolute_salinity': 'YlGnBu_r', 'sigma0': 'BuPu', 'AOU': 'RdBu_r'}))

The render defaults — byte-identical to the former plots.py module globals.
